title: Boston Dynamics adds wheels to Atlas humanoid to test whole-body control
summary: Boston Dynamics combines classical motor control with whole-body reinforcement learning to power dynamic, wheeled locomotion for Atlas.
points: Bridging the divide between deterministic physics-based control and policy-driven adaptation, Boston Dynamics released a video today showing its Atlas humanoid using wheels to move around.
The “experiment” combined classical model-based motor control with whole-body reinforcement learning to maintain dynamic stability across unstructured, real-world terrain.
In the video, Andy Wu, controls engineer for Atlas at Boston Dynamics, highlights some recent experiments that he executed by attaching wheels to Atlas’ legs.

title: PrimeBOT Builds Its 10,000th Personal Robot, 14 Days After Its 5,000th
summary: PrimeBOT says its 10,000th Q1 and T1 personal robot rolled off the line on November 8, with daily capacity at 240 units. It has not disclosed sales or deliveries.
points: PrimeBOT, the personal-robot brand of Shanghai-listed Swancor Advanced Materials, said its 10,000th robot came off the production line on November 8.

title: Atlas Battery Pack to Use 70 Samsung SDI Cells, Report Says
summary: The reported 1.3 kWh pack adds detail to Atlas’s power system as humanoid makers pursue battery swapping, fast charging and new chemistries.
points: Samsung SDI is supplying the battery cells for Boston Dynamics’ Atlas humanoid, with each robot using 70 cylindrical cells in a pack of approximately 1.3 kWh, according to The Elec .
The report offers a closer look at the power supply behind Atlas as robot manufacturers pursue different ways to keep their machines working through an industrial shift.
The reported cells have a capacity of 5,000 mAh each and use the 2170 format: 21 mm in diameter and 70 mm long.
